summary: Design safeguarding controls, reporting routes and partner checks. Practise survivor-centred response and board oversight in this five-day course.
lede: Organisational safeguarding training helps NGO, humanitarian, HR and programme leads build systems to prevent harm and respond to concerns. Participants practise mapping risks, responsibilities, reporting routes and referral pathways, while developing workflows for safe triage and survivor-centred responses. They also learn to assess partner controls and prepare confidential oversight reporting using de-identified information.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for people who set safeguarding controls, handle concerns, oversee services or hold partners accountable in NGOs, humanitarian agencies, schools, healthcare organisations and donor-funded programmes.
modules: IASC Principles and Codes of Conduct
prerequisites: No specialist investigation qualification is required. Familiarity with your organisation’s reporting lines, programmes or safeguarding policies will help you apply the exercises. Coding is not required; digital work uses spreadsheet-based safeguarding data examples. Advanced investigation and case-management topics receive operational-level coverage, while practical exercises focus on system design, triage, documentation and oversight.
